title: Flat bar with opposite U-notches in tension, t = 10 mm, r = 4 mm
description:
Flat steel bar with two opposite U-notches, in tension. Plane stress.
Geometry file (STEP): the planar outline of the bar in the xy-plane (the thickness is not modelled in the STEP).
Purpose: a 5 mm thick flat tension strap, 200 mm long (x from -100 mm to 100 mm) and H = 50 mm wide (y from -25 mm to 25 mm), with two opposite U-shaped notches at mid-length (x = 0), one in each long edge. Each notch is 10 mm deep measured from the edge, has parallel flanks 8 mm apart and a semicircular root of radius r = 4 mm; the net width between the notch roots is 30 mm.
Material: steel, linear elastic and isotropic, E = 200 GPa, Poisson's ratio 0.3. Thickness 5 mm (plane stress).
Supports: the end x = -100 mm is held in the x direction only (free to contract in y; a frictionless support); remove the remaining rigid-body motion (y translation) with a constraint that does not stress the bar.
Load: a total tensile force P = 20 kN in +x, applied as a uniform traction on the end x = 100 mm.
Analysis: linear static, small displacements.
Report:
  peak_stress_notch: the maximum value of the maximum principal stress s1 on the semicircular notch roots [Pa];
  elongation: the average x-displacement of the loaded end x = 100 mm [m].
